p: his angels: Because they are members of the same body, he sets them before our eyes, who are most willing and by their prompt obedience teach us to do our duty.
sun and moon: In that God's glory shines in these insensible creatures, this their beauty is as a continual praising of God.
heavens of heavens: Not that there are various heavens, but because of the spheres and of the situation of the fixed stars and planets, he comprehends by this word the whole heavens.
waters that be above the heavens: That is, the rain which is in the middle region of the air, which he here comprehends under the name of the heavens.
dragons: Meaning the great and monstrous fishes, as whales and such like.
Fire: Which come not by chance or fortune, but by God's appointed ordinance.

Kings of the earth: For the greater gifts that any has received and the more high that one is preferred, the more bound is he to praise God for the same: but neither high nor low condition or degree can be exempted from this duty.
horn of his people: That is, the dignity, power and glory of his Church.
children of Israel: By reason of his covenant made with Abraham.
